S79.01.note: The same Auto row opens from the model name button above the message box (testID chat.composer.model); that button shows no fixed visible word.
steps: Tap the menu icon at the top left of the chat screen (Open navigation drawer).
Tap Settings, then General, then Models.
Tap the row Auto at the top of the list.
Go back to the chat, send a message, and read the answer's footer (provider · model) to see which model answered.
Compare with Expected: Auto should pick a model for the request from the registry.
S79.01.where: Open navigation drawer > Settings > General > Models > Auto

S79.02.needs: a Cloud account for cloud models (a Free account can choose Free models)
steps: Tap the menu icon at the top left (Open navigation drawer).
Tap Settings, then General, then Models.
Under Selected model, tap a named model row that is not Auto.
Go back to the chat, send a message, and read the footer under the answer.
Compare with Expected: the footer should show the chosen model, not a different one.
S79.02.where: Open navigation drawer > Settings > General > Models > pick a specific model row

S79.03.needs: a Cloud account and a project whose default model was set on the web app
S79.03.note: Mobile shows and applies the project default model but has no control to set it; the mobile update call only changes icon and accent colour.
steps: Tap the menu icon at the top left (Open navigation drawer).
Under Projects, tap a Cloud project.
Read the line Default model: on the project's details.
Tap New chat inside that project and check the model it opens with.
Compare with Expected: a new chat in the project should use the project's default model.
S79.03.where: Open navigation drawer > Projects > tap a project > Default model:

S79.04.note: The task-specific profile is set in the routing registry (autoProfileByTask, coding maps to premium); no mobile control sets it. The line appears only when the answering model differs from the requested one.
steps: Select Auto as the model (see S79.01).
Send a coding or reasoning request, for example a small function to write.
Read the line under the answer that starts with Auto chose, if it appears.
S79.04.where: Inside Auto; visible as the line Auto chose under an answer when Auto moves to another model

S79.08.note: No privacy-first profile control found in apps/mobile. Searched for zero retention, retention and privacy profile. Nearest controls: the Local / Cloud switch in the drawer (ModeToggle, accessibility label Local Mode, apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ModeToggle.tsx) and Settings > Privacy > Data retention (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-privacy/index.tsx).

S79.09.note: Intent classification has no control; the code is in packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts.
steps: Select Auto and send two different requests, one simple and one that needs a specialised task.
Compare the footer model under each answer, and any Auto chose line.
S79.09.where: Inner routing step; effect only visible as the Auto chose line when Auto switches model

S79.10.note: The tool control is shown as Active chat tools in apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ChatInput.tsx (accessibility label only), so the label is not a visible word.
steps: Turn on a chat tool such as search or a code tool from the chat tools control.
Send a request that needs that tool, then read the footer under the answer for the model used.
S79.10.where: Inner routing step; no visible control; effect appears only in the chosen model

S79.11.needs: a photo to attach and a Cloud account
S79.11.note: Modality classification is in packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts and has no control of its own.
steps: Select Auto, attach a photo to the message, and ask about it.
Read the footer under the answer for the model that answered, and check that it can read images.
S79.11.where: Inner routing step; effect visible as the model in the footer under the answer

S79.12.note: The effort controls in the picker are chosen by the user and are not the routing classification.
steps: Send a very short question and then a long multi-step question with Auto selected.
Compare the footer model under each answer.
S79.12.where: Inner routing step; no visible control

S79.13.needs: a Cloud account and an internet connection
S79.13.note: Freshness detection has no visible control; the routing code is in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts.
steps: Select Auto and ask about a current event, for example today's news.
Check that the answer shows current information and read the footer for the model used.
S79.13.where: Inner routing step; effect visible as an answer that uses current information

S79.14.needs: a Free account, to see locked rows
S79.14.note: The locked-row message is an accessibility hint in apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/components/ModelRow.tsx, not visible text, so no exact visible label was found.
steps: Open the model picker from Settings > General > Models.
Look for rows that are locked or unavailable and compare them with the models your plan includes.
S79.14.where: Inner filter applied before ranking; effect visible in the model picker list

S79.15.note: Only the model is shown in the footer under each answer, not the provider route.
S79.15.where: Server-side route choice; no mobile screen shows which provider route served the answer

steps: Open Settings > General > Models and pick a specific model that is not Auto.
Send a message, then read the footer under the answer.
Check the footer shows the same model and that no Auto chose line appears.
S79.16.where: Picking a specific model keeps that model; effect visible in the answer footer

labels.text: Available while the provider-funded quota lasts.

S79.19.needs: a Free account or a Cloud account with a limited plan
S79.19.note: The quota text is the description of a Free quota model; the budget check itself is not shown to the user.
steps: Note the remaining usage shown in the app, then send several requests with Auto selected.
Check the footer model under each answer as the usage is used up.
S79.19.where: Server-side route choice that considers remaining budget; no mobile control

S79.20.note: The fallback runs in apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts; it cannot be forced from the app, so reproduction is not dependable.
steps: Send a message with Auto selected and read the footer model.
Repeat during a provider outage if one is known, and check the footer shows a working model.
S79.20.where: Server-side fallback when a route fails; effect visible only as a different footer model

S79.21.needs: a Cloud account, a photo to attach, and an image model that cannot edit
S79.21.note: The offer exists only for blocked image-edit requests (alertBlockedImageRequest.ts); other plan blocks show a Choose model banner instead, which is not a switch offer.
steps: Tap Add to chat and attach a photo.
Choose an image model that cannot edit images, then send an edit request.
Read the alert and check whether it offers Use <model name> beside Cancel.
Tap Use <model name> and check that the image model changes.
Compare with Expected: the switch is offered as a one-tap choice.
S79.21.where: Chat composer > Add to chat (attach an image) > send an image edit request with an image model that cannot edit it > Use <model name> in the alert

steps: Open a chat in Cloud mode.
Tap the message box and type /.
Tap compare, which reads Compare model responses.
On the Compare Models screen, choose a model for each slot and send one prompt.
Compare the two answers side by side with Expected.
S79.24.where: Chat (Cloud mode) > message box > type / > compare (Compare model responses) > Compare Models

S79.26.note: The line appears only when the answering model differs from the requested one, so it may not show on every answer.
steps: Select Auto and send a question.
Wait for the answer to finish.
Read the line under the answer that starts with Auto chose, with the reason after it.
Compare with Expected: the line should say why Auto picked or moved to a model.
S79.26.where: Chat > ask a question > read the line under the answer that starts Auto chose

S79.27.note: The footer is hidden while the answer is still streaming.
steps: Send any message in a chat.
Wait for the answer to finish streaming.
Read the small grey footer under the answer, which shows provider and model.
Compare with Expected: the model named in the footer should be the one that answered.
S79.27.where: Chat > send a message > read the footer under the answer (provider · model)

S79.28.note: Searched apps/mobile for routing policy version and trace; only the server-side trace in packages/ai/routing/src/routing-trace.ts and apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/routing-decision-trace-service.ts exist.
S79.28.where: Not visible in the mobile app; the routing trace is recorded on the server

S79.30.note: A failed classification cannot be forced from the app, so the effect is hard to reproduce on demand.
steps: Send an unusual or ambiguous message with Auto selected.
Check the answer still arrives and read the footer for the model used.
S79.30.where: Server-side fallback to a safe default when classification fails; no visible control
